subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should OpenClaw core expose durable session archive/rotation events as cron triggers, or should this remain a plugin/session_end integration pattern?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix would add public cron/config/protocol surface and can launch unattended agent turns from session-state changes, so automation should not choose the security and product boundary.

options.title: Add Narrow Core Event Trigger
options.body: Define a durable session lifecycle event schedule for cron with scoped metadata, idempotency, permissions, trace records, and tests across reset/rotation paths.

options.title: Keep It Plugin-Owned
options.body: Treat session_end plugin hooks as the supported integration point and document how a plugin can run post-session automation without adding cron event schedules.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Cron Hooks
options.body: Track this as a subcase of the broader cron hook lifecycle design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/9465 before adding any new schema.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Core Event Trigger
recommendation.body: Define a durable session lifecycle event schedule for cron with scoped metadata, idempotency, permissions, trace records, and tests across reset/rotation paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history across cron, Gateway, and product/security review surfaces for this decision.
